Where the open edges of the wall of 200 m lie, measured by cutting its windows one after another
with the recipe the skipped test holds and listing the edges that have not one use each way after
each cut.

| What | Measure |
|---|---|
| Open edges after the 25th cut | 3, which close a triangle |
| The triangle's corners | (12.47273, 1.5, 0.2), (12.95, 1.49993, 0.2) and (13.35, 1.5, 0.2) |
| Its sides | 0.877 m, 0.400 m and 0.477 m |
| Its height over the longest side | 7e-5 m |
| Cuts after which the wall is open | the 11th, 14th, 20th, 21st, 22nd and 25th, each with 3 edges |
| Cuts after which it is closed | the other 19 |

The triangle lies on the front face, along the top line of a window at y = 1.5, which the corner at
x = 12.95 has left by 7e-5 m. Its height is under the join's distance, 1e-4 m, while its area is
far over the partition's 1e-12, so the partition keeps it where the join would take its three
points for a line. The count of vertices within 1e-3 m of the top line but off it grows with the
cuts, 1 after the 3rd, 3 after the 10th, 5 after the 14th and 6 after the 25th, so the drift is
in the windows' corners and not in one cut. The wall is closed again after the 12th cut and the
23rd, so what is open depends on the faces a cut happens to make of the front, which this
measure does not follow further.
